answer.rationale: Competitive price cuts demand a response, but memory_73 clearly flags that promotional pricing materially reduces 30-day retention and should not be generalized—this is precisely the trap that destroys long-term qualified revenue. Referral incentives (memory_57) work well for established customers but won't address immediate churn in price-sensitive new/early SMB accounts. Enterprise sales assist and onboarding simplification are orthogonal to the immediate retention crisis. Activation messaging (memory_91) improved week-one engagement and first meaningful action; paired with the proven onboarding shortening (memory_86), this combination can accelerate SMB time-to-value and deepen product stickiness without eroding retention or margin. A small guarded test on churning/at-risk SMB cohorts lets us validate whether faster value realization + reinforced activation nudges can compete against price without the long-term damage of discounting. This preserves the option to escalate to referral or sales assist if messaging alone proves insufficient, while avoiding the retention cliff that memory_73 documented.
